phase-plan.purpose: Harden the Payload-backed content editor into a real import/export/publish loop: add custom-schema and docs-site platform collections, publish project data back into engine JSON/source files, run codegen/build artifacts, apply the required DB migrations, and bootstrap canonical game data into the DB.
phase-plan.scope: In scope: new Payload collections and migration, authoring service publish flow, publish/bootstrap routes/scripts, minimal content-app publish controls, bootstrap import of canonical pack data, and architecture/planning updates. Out of scope: rich per-pack editing UI, revision history, validation report views, and Supabase delivery APIs.

file.description: Project-scoped custom schema definitions that extend canonical game packs.
Docs-site and Payload authoring platform extension records, fixed to the docs-site/Payload authoring layer.
Import/export/publish service that writes project docs back into engine contracts and rebuilds engine/KAPLAY artifacts.
API route for explicit project publish back into the game content pipeline.
Repeatable command that creates/reuses a content project, imports canonical engine packs, and optionally publishes.
Migration for the custom schema and platform data collections.
Architecture doc updated with the working Payload import/export/publish loop and seeded DB state.

task.description: Add custom-schema and platform-data Payload collections plus migration/type generation support.
Implement project publish flow that exports project files, syncs engine source/data JSON, and rebuilds engine/KAPLAY artifacts.
Add a reusable bootstrap command and use it to seed/import the canonical engine pack set into Payload DB.

decision.summary: Platform-data rows are fixed to the docs-site/Payload authoring platform and categorized by namespace, not by arbitrary runtime consumer choice.
decision.impact: Prevents the editor from conflating authoring-platform metadata with game-runtime content delivery targets.

decision.summary: Published Payload project docs write back into the same engine contract files the game already consumes, then run the existing engine and KAPLAY build pipeline.
decision.impact: Keeps the DB-backed authoring loop aligned to the actual runtime file system instead of creating a second data source.
